plain: Having no good reason behind it

webster.text: Wanting ground or foundation; wanting cause or reason for support; as groundless fear.

more.text: Not authorized; false; as a groundless report or assertion.

example.quote: I conceive, sir, that this is a very plain case, and that it must appear perfectly clear to the committee that the gentleman's alarms are groundless.
example.cite: Jonathan Elliot, ed., The Debates in the Several State Conventions on the Adoption of the Federal Constitution, vol. 4, North Carolina Convention, Mr. DAVIE, July 29, 1788 (2d ed. 1836)
